The L1-convergent truncations are separately affine with nonnegative slopes in each independent U_i, so finite coordinate convex-order replacement and the Lipschitz stop-loss limit prove the unrestricted convex-order comparison of V. Multiplication by independent Z² preserves it for X². The generator recurrence gives EX²=2D/[r(1-u)], standardized fourth moment 6(1-u)/(1-E U²); strict Jensen and chord equality give unique deterministic and {0,1} endpoints. The opposite p<2 versus p>2 moment rankings and density-at-origin ordering follow by convexity/concavity of the appropriate variance power. Our separate exact Fraction computations checked x²=15/7 and three kurtosis normalizations; finite checks do not replace the infinite-perpetuity argument.
